Bethphage. It is not certain whether it was a village or a district; but most probably it was a village between Bethany and Jerusalem, and on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives.  The latter was separated from Jerusalem by the valley of the Kidron.

title: Matthew 21:2
text: An ass tied, and a colt. Mark and Luke mention only the colt.  The latter would be more suitable for this occasion.  See  Mark 11:2 I Samuel 6:7 .

title: Matthew 21:3
text: Straightway he will send them. Most probably the owner of the two animals was a secret disciple of Jesus.

title: Matthew 21:5
text: Riding upon an ass. After the manner of a king of peace.  In selecting an ass whereon to ride Jesus consciously fulfilled the prophecy of Zechariah.

title: Matthew 21:7
text: He sat thereon. On the garments of clothes placed upon the back of the colt.

title: Matthew 21:8
text: Spread their garments. An unusual tribute of admiration and devotion, such as was sometimes paid to great religious teachers among the Jews, or to great rulers.

title: Matthew 21:9
text:
Hosanna. The Greek form of a Hebrew word meaning 'save now' ( Psalms 118:25 ).  It had come to be an expression meaning 'praise' or 'honor.'
 

 
To the Son of David. A joyous acknowledgement that Jesus was the Messiah.

title: Matthew 21:10
text: When he was come into Jerusalem. The triumphal entry into Jerusalem took place on the ninth day of Nisan, the first month of the Jewish year, and nearly corresponding to our April.  The day is known to Christians as Palm Sunday.

title: Matthew 21:12
text:
Jesus entered into the temple. This took place on the day following the entry into the city ( Mark 11:11 ).
 

 
All them that sold and bought. There was a market in the Court of the Gentiles for the sale of sheep and oxen and whatever else was necessary for the Temple sacrifices and service.
 

 
The tables of the money-changers. The money tribute of a half-shekel due at this time from male Israelites had to be paid in Jewish coins.  Roman and other coins were exchanged for these, and the amount of the commission profits had grown into an abuse.

title: Matthew 21:15
text: The children. Only Matthew mentions this.

title: Matthew 21:19
text: Immediately the fig tree withered. According to Mark this miracle was performed on Monday morning, but the disciples did not see the withered tree until the following morning ( Mark 11:12-14 Mark 16:20 ).  Those who see in this an evidence of Christ's anger apparently forget that it was wrought upon a tree, while his miracles of deliverance and compassion were all wrought in behalf of mankind.

title: Matthew 21:21
text: Be thou taken up. It was the oriental way of speaking: an emphatic expression for something very difficult.  See  Matthew 17:20 Luke 17:6 I Corinthians 13:2 .

title: Matthew 21:23
text:
By what authority. Jesus had not been ordained as a rabbi.
 

 
These things. His triumphal entry into the city, the driving out of the money-changers and the miracles of healing the lame and blind, etc.  The question also referred to the claim of Jesus as Messiah and to the whole character of his mission and teaching.

title: Matthew 21:27
text: We know not. A humiliating confession of ignorance from those whose duty it was to be able to answer such a question.  They were expected, as members of the Sanhedrin, to decide between true and false prophets.

title: Matthew 21:32
text: In the way of righteousness. Of the righteousness of the law, and as such not objectionable to the Pharisees.

title: Matthew 21:33
text:
:44
 
Hear another parable. The parable of the wicked husbandmen was a direct reproof to the chief priests and elders as conspirators who were seeking the death of Christ.  In it the householder represents God; the son, Christ; the servants, Moses and the prophets the husbandmen, the Pharisees and scribes, teachers of the people.  Christ as the son of the householder, claims to be the Son of God, thus giving his accusers the final answer to their question as to the authority by which he preached and wrought miracles.
 

 
 They say. Here the accusers of Jesus in their own answer acknowledged the puunishment that was coming upon here and the Jewish nation.

title: Matthew 21:46
text: When they sought to lay hold on him. Indicating their fixed purpose to kill him, since they could neither diminish the enthusiasm for him among the multitudes nor silence him by argument.  They were undoubtedly acting for the Sanhedrin, whose object was to seize Jesus as quickly as possible and as quietly, for the vengeance of Christ's Galilean followers was feared.  This was why they made use of the treachery of Judas.

title: Matthew 22:2
text: A certain king. In this parable of the royal marriage feast ( Matthew 22:1-14 ) Jesus repeats the truths and warnings of the preceding one.  God is meant by 'a certain king;' the 'servants' are the apostles; the 'rest,' or the remnant, are the chief priests, scribes and Pharisees.

title: Matthew 22:7
text: Burned their city. Jerusalem is meant.

title: Matthew 22:9
text: The partings of the highways. The territory of the Gentiles.  Since the Jews, the bidden guests, would not come to the marriage feast, the servants were to invite as many as they could find both bad and good.

title: Matthew 22:11
text: A man who had not on a wedding-garment. A serious offence according to eastern etiquette, and in the parable one that could easily have been avoided, as the king had provided a wedding garment for each of his guests.  The meaning is plain.  The wedding-garment is a righteous life, which alone gives the right to appear at the wedding feast.  The guests were judged.  Those who had the garment were accepted; he who was without it was condemned.

title: Matthew 22:14
text: Many are called, but few chosen. Referring most probably to the Jews of Christ's time.  Few were chosen because few responded to the call.  See  Matthew 20:16 .

title: Matthew 22:15
text: Took counsel. Our Lord's replies were so exasperating to his accusers that the latter were resolved at all hazards to exhaust their ingenuity before giving up the attempt to entrap him in his own words.

title: Matthew 22:16
text: The Herodians. Partisans of the royal family of Herod.  They naturally strove to please the Romans and were unfriendly to the Pharisees.  Nevertheless the latter called them to their aid as being especially serviceable in case Jesus should give an entangling answer to a political question.

title: Matthew 22:21
text: Render therefore unto Caesar the things, etc. An argument against the union of church and state.  Each has its own duties and these are to be kept apart.  The Jews were commanded to obey Caesar in political matters, but to worship God in their religion.  In the latter respect Jesus defied Caesar, as in the former he upheld his authority.

title: Matthew 22:22
text: Marveled, and left him. The reply was altogether above and beyond their petty religious and political notions.  It showed how a universal religion could be made possible by separating it from any narrow national restrictions.

title: Matthew 22:29
text: Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures. The Sadducees, disbelieving in the resurrection, naturally sought to make light of it.  They were mistaken in supposing that if persons rose from the dead they would meet with conditions similar to those of the earthly life.

title: Matthew 22:30
text: As angels. This was a rebuke to the Sadducees in their denial of the existence of angels ( Acts 23:8 ).  See  Luke 20:36 .

title: Matthew 22:31
text: Spoken unto you by God. That is, in the book of Exodus, a part of the Mosaic law in which they believed.

title: Matthew 22:38
text: The great and first commandment. It is probable that the Pharisee who asked this question did not do so in a hostile spirit.  At least it does not appear so from  Mark 12:28 Luke 10:25 .  Most likely it was intended as a fair test.  The reply of Jesus in  Mark 12:34  shows that he was pleased with his questioner.

title: Matthew 22:39
text: Love they neighbor as thyself. Not as a man ordinarily does love himself, that is, selfishly, but as he should love himself.

title: Matthew 22:42
text: The Christ. The Messiah.

title: Matthew 22:44
text:
Lord. God or Jehovah.
 

 
My Lord. The Lord of David, the Messiah that was to come.

title: Matthew 22:45
text: How is he his son? The reply of the Pharisees, acknowledging that the Christ, or Messiah, was the Son of David, was only partly acceptable to Jesus.  The psalm quoted by him in  Matthew 22:44  implies that the Christ is also Lord of David and that he has a right to sit at the right hand of God.  Thus did Jesus prove to the Pharisees the divine authority of the Christ as Messiah from a psalm, which they fully accepted as Messianic.

title: Matthew 23:2
text: Sit on Moses' seat. Referring to the power of judging and teaching, which they received by the laying on of hands at their ordination ceremony.

title: Matthew 23:3
text: All things therefore. Jesus recognizes the right of the scribes and Pharisees to be loyally obeyed until the incoming of the new dispensation.

title: Matthew 23:4
text: Heavy burdens. Minute and perplexing interpretations of the law.  See  Matthew 11:30 .

title: Matthew 23:5
text:
Phylacteries. Small boxes made out of calfskin, containing little rolls on which were written these four portions of the Mosaic law:  Exodus 13:1-16 Deuteronomy 4:4-9 Deuteronomy 11:13-21 .  They were attached to a broad strip of leather or other material, and were used at prayer-time.  One was worn on the brow between the eyes and in each of its four small compartments one of the four passages from the law was enclosed, inscribed on a bit of parchment.  The other was worn on the inside of the left arm, and hidden by the sleeve.  The scripture passages in this were on a single roll.  Making broad the phylacteries came to be known as an external sign of piety.  Jesus rebukes the scribes and Pharisees for their pretentious use of them.
 

 
The borders. The fringes on the cloak or outer garment, and fastened to it by a blue ribbon.  See  Numbers 15:38 .  The Pharisees wore the fringes wider than others.

title: Matthew 23:7
text: Rabbi. Aramaic for 'My Master,' the usual manner of addressing a scribe or teacher of the law.

title: Matthew 23:9
text: Father. This was also a title sometimes given to the scribes.  'Father' and 'master' are not condemned by Jesus as names.  He denounces the spiritual arrogance and conceit of the religious leaders who shelter themselves under such names.

title: Matthew 23:13
text: Because ye shut the kingdom of heaven against men. The first of the seven woes against the scribes and Pharisees.  It alludes to the hiding of the truth by outward ceremonies and false teaching, thereby keeping men out of the kingdom of heaven.

title: Matthew 23:15
text:
Compass. Travel over or about  Matthew 4:23 Matthew 9:35 .
 

 
Proselyte. A new convert.

title: Matthew 23:16
text: The gold of the temple. Gold brought as an offering or gift; the 'Corban' or 'devoted,' the saying of which word bound the giver as by an oath.

title: Matthew 23:23
text: Tithe mint and anise and cummin. The Jews were commanded to give a tenth part of the fruit of the field and the trees as an offering ( Leviticus 27:30 ).  The small and unimportant garden herbs were likewise included in the tithe by the Pharisees in their excessive zeal for minute regulations.  Cummin was used as a spice in cooking.

title: Matthew 23:24
text: Strain out the gnat. Out of the wine that was to be drunk.

title: Matthew 23:27
text: Whited sepulchres. The Jews whitewashed the graves of their dead in order to avoid the ceremonial defilement resulting from walking over them.

title: Matthew 23:31
text: Ye witness to yourselves. If those whom Jesus rebuked had lived in the time of their fathers, they would have slain the prophets as their fathers did.

title: Matthew 23:32
text: Fill ye up then. Proceed with your evil designs, as your fathers did, and slay also this prophet sent to you from God.

title: Matthew 23:34
text: I send unto you prophets, etc.  Here Jesus refers to his apostles, prophets, teachers and evangelists, but he gives them Jewish titles.  See  Luke 11:49-51 .

title: Matthew 23:35
text:
Upon you. Upon the scribes and Pharisees as leaders of the people.
 

 
All the righteous blood. The penalty for shedding it.

title: Matthew 23:37
text: How often. The words suggest that Jesus had frequently preached and ministered in Jerusalem.

title: Matthew 23:38
text: Your house. The city itself.

title: Matthew 23:39
text: Till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh. The verse closes the last public discourse of Jesus.

title: Matthew 24:1
text: The buildings of the temple. Herod's Temple had not at this time been completed ( John 2:20 ).

title: Matthew 24:2
text: One stone. The prediction of the Temple's destruction was literally fulfilled.  The whole building was laid even with the ground.

title: Matthew 24:3
text: Came unto him privately. Peter, James, John and Andrew are meant ( Mark 13:3 ).

title: Matthew 24:4
text: Take heed. This warning opens a discourse to the disciples which is in  Matthew 24:4-25:46 .

title: Matthew 24:5
text: Shall come in my name. Among such pretenders who appeared before the destruction of Jerusalem were Simon Magus, Dositheus and Menander.

title: Matthew 24:16
text: Flee unto the mountains. Many Christians fled to Pella in Perea during the siege of Jerusalem.

title: Matthew 24:22
text: Those days. The days of the siege, whose horrors were so great that only their being shortened allowed any to escape.  Jerusalem was captured by the Romans on August 10, A.D. 70.

title: Matthew 24:26
text: In the wilderness. A false Christ or prophet might strive to lure people after him by an ascetic life.

title: Matthew 24:29
text: The sun shall be darkened, etc.  The striking and figurative expressions contained in  Matthew 24:29-31  are characteristic of scripture prophecy, especially in the Old Testament.

title: Matthew 24:32
text: From the fig tree. This parable has been interpreted to mean the coming of the kingdom of heaven.

title: Matthew 24:37
text: As were the days of Noah. See  Luke 17:27-29 .

title: Matthew 24:41
text: Two women shall be grinding. The custom of women grinding grain with handmills is alluded to.  In Palestine these mills are still in common use where there are no mill streams.

title: Matthew 24:42
text: Watch therefore: for ye know not on what day. An argument as well as a command.  The uncertainty of the Lord's coming will not permit any lack of vigilance.

title: Matthew 24:43
text: If the master of the house had known. The bitter reflection of all who neglect their duty and lament the resulting loss and punishment.  This truth is brought home by three parables: the wise servant, the ten virgins and the talents.

title: Matthew 24:45
text: Whom his lord hath set over his household. This was a servant who was promoted to be a steward, a reward of fidelity and discretion.  The position called for the ability of a manager and the honesty of a faithful trustee.

title: Matthew 24:47
text: Over all that he hath. Still further promotion; he now has charge of all his lord's affairs.

title: Matthew 24:48
text: Shall say in his heart. In the promptings of a heart that is unfaithful begins the failure of watchfulness.  The evil servant thought he could speculate on the time of his lord's return.  He was in danger from the moment when he said, My Lord tarrieth.

title: Matthew 25:1
text:
Then. In the time of the judgment.  This is another parable about watchfulness.
 

 
To meet the bridegroom. It was the custom at a Jewish wedding for the bridegroom's friends to escort the bride to the threshold of her husband's home.  When the threshold was reached, the bridegroom led the bride across it.  In this parable the bridegroom himself went to bring his bride, and the virgins awaited his return.

title: Matthew 25:2
text: Were wise. Here the wisdom was shown in a form of watchfulness, a preparation for meeting the bridegroom in the proper manner when he came.

title: Matthew 25:9
text: There will not be enough for us and you. The foolish virgins had some oil, that is, a certain degree of preparation; they lacked the thoroughness and persistence that fully provided for the coming event.

title: Matthew 25:10
text: While they went away to buy. The test of watchfulness came in the very moment when they were hurrying to make good their lack of prudence.

title: Matthew 25:15
text: Five talents. The parable of the talents is only in the Gospel according to Matthew.  Like the two preceding, it is a parable of watchfulness, but there are also thoughts on the use of time while waiting and watching.  The fact is emphasized that difference in natural gifts is less important than the careful cultivation by each one of such talents as have been bestowed.  See  Luke 19:11-28  for differences between the parable of the talents and the parable of the pounds.

title: Matthew 25:18
text: He that received the one went away. His thought was similar to that of the evil servant in the parable of the wise steward.  He had put out of his mind the need of watchful provision against his lord's return.  He did worse, in deliberately neglecting the trust reposed in him.

title: Matthew 25:23
text: Enter thou into the joy of they lord. Partake of the happiness of thy lord, the reward which thy faithfulness has earned.

title: Matthew 25:24
text: Lord I knew thee that thou art a hard man. His excuse begins with a falsehood                     which proves to be a trap, for his lord takes him at his word and condemns him because he did not prepare to meet the requirements of a hard man who reaped where he sowed not.  It was easy for this servant to have entrusted his lord's money to responsible persons.

title: Matthew 25:28
text: Take ye away therefore. Gifts unused become worthless.  This is the lesson of the lord's sentence upon the slothful servant.  It holds good in all walks of life.

title: Matthew 25:33
text:
The sheep. The righteous, set on the right hand.  The words 'right' and 'left' in this connection have the same meaning in the Hebrew and Greek languages.  Those on the right are the righteous; those on the left, the wicked.  See  Deuteronomy 33:2 Proverbs 3:16 .
 

 
 The goats. The wicked.

title: Matthew 25:34
text:
The King. Christ.  Afterward he also acknowledges himself king before Pilate ( Matthew 27:11 ).
 

 
Inherit the kingdom. As sons of God coming to their own.

title: Matthew 25:35
text: For I was hungry. Christ, the judge of those before him rewards them according to their acts.  It has often been pointed out that the good deeds for which Christ rewards his faithful increase in their self-sacrificing quality up to the last of those here enumerated.  To satisfy hunger and thirst, or to give lodging to a stranger is the mark of a charitable and well-disposed person; but, though meritorious, it calls for less self-denial than clothing the naked or visiting those who are sick and in prison.

title: Matthew 25:40
text: Inasmuch as ye did it unto one of these. Here is declared the great distinctive motive of Christian service.  The things done for mankind, even the least of men and women and children, are done for Christ and are so accepted by him.

title: Matthew 26:2
text: The Son of man is delivered up. An emphatic prediction of the betrayal found only in Matthew.

title: Matthew 26:3
text:
Then were gathered together. Probably an informal gathering of the great council, the Sanhedrin.
 

 
The court of the high priest. The central quadrangle around which the palace was built.
 

 
Caiaphas. Joseph Caiaphas, son-in-law of Annas.  He was appointed high priest in A.D. 26 by the Roman procurator Valerius Gratus.

title: Matthew 26:6
text: Simon the leper. Simon's disease must have been cured, otherwise he would not have been allowed to have guests in his house.

title: Matthew 26:7
text:
A woman having an alabaster cruse. Mary, the sister of Lazarus ( John 12:2 John 12:3 ).  The cruse was a vase with a long neck.
 

 
Exceeding precious. The ointment was worth about $150.

title: Matthew 26:12
text: To prepare me for burial. Another prediction of his death.

title: Matthew 26:13
text: That also which this woman hath done. Mary's act won higher praise from Jesus than any other mentioned in the New Testament.  It was a most touching proof of devotion, and a sign of recognition of Christ's true nature and work.  The anointing has had a place in the Christian consciousness ever since and will have unto the end of time.

title: Matthew 26:15
text: Willing to give. The motive was greed.  See  John 12:6 .

title: Matthew 26:17
text: On the first day of unleavened bread. The Feast of Unleavened Bread began on the 14th of Nisan, the first month of the Jewish year, in the evening, that is, in the beginning of the 15th day.  It was popularly identified with the Passover.

title: Matthew 26:18
text:
Such a man. Probably a disciple who had been informed and who was ready and willing to do what was required of him.
 

 
My time is at hand. The time of his betrayal and crucifixion.

title: Matthew 26:24
text: Good were it for that man, etc.  An expression often used among the Jews in condemnation of one who knew the law, and did not obey it.

title: Matthew 26:25
text: Thou hast said. A common form of assent in Palestine.

title: Matthew 26:26
text: And as they were eating, Jesus took the bread. The institution of the Last Supper is recorded in  Matthew 26:26-29 .  See  Mark 14:22 Luke 22:19 I Corinthians 11:23-25 .  It was on the 14th, which began after sunset on the 13th of Nisan.  In  Matthew 26:18  the words 'I keep the Passover at thy house' may be taken as spoken by our Lord with the intention of following the ritual of the Passover as far as possible.  That would be according to his declaration that he came to fulfill the law; but on the other hand he was instituting a new rite to be observed by his followers for all time, so that the Passover ritual would, if necessary, be modified.  Some think there was no paschal lamb, Christ himself being offered as a sacrifice, doing away forever with the necessity of the typical lamb without blemish.

title: Matthew 26:28
text:
This is my blood. The wine poured from the cup was a symbol of the blood shed for the remission of sins.
 

 
For many. Mankind.

title: Matthew 26:30
text: When they had sung a hymn. The second part of the Hallel ( Psalms 115:1-118:29 ).  'Hallel' meaning praise, was a term of the Hebrew religious service applied to certain psalms, especially to those above indicated.

title: Matthew 26:32
text: I will go before you into Galilee. That is, I will lead you as a shepherd into Galilee.  Jesus after again predicting his resurrection, continues in these words the figure of a shepherd going before his flock, in harmony with Zechariah's prophecy quoted in  Matthew 26:31 .  The disciples were to meet in Galilee.  See  Matthew 28:16 John 21:1-25 I Corinthians 15:6 .

title: Matthew 26:33
text: But Peter answered. Impulsive arrogance here characterized the words of Peter as on former occasions.  He declared in effect that his loyalty and affection for his Master were deeper than those of the other apostles.

title: Matthew 26:34
text: Before the cock crow. Before dawn.  Mark says: Before the cock crow twice ( Matthew 14:30 ).  The two expressions practically mean the same, as the cock crows at frequent intervals in the early morning.

title: Matthew 26:35
text: Even if I must die with thee, etc.  Peter's sinful presumption and audacity increased even after Jesus warned him.  Hence the humiliation of his denial was correspondingly deep.

title: Matthew 26:36
text: Gethsemane. Literally, 'the oil press'.  It was at the foot of the western slope of the Mount of Olives, and was probably an olive yard.  Like all the other gardens of Jerusalem, it was outside the city walls.

title: Matthew 26:37
text: Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. Peter, James and John were closest to Jesus and were better fitted than the others to witness his agony in the garden.  They had been with him on the Mount of Transfiguration.

title: Matthew 26:39
text: Not as I will. The human nature of our Lord sought deliverance from his coming trial, yet he submitted to the will of his Father.

title: Matthew 26:40
text: Saith unto Peter. As Peter was first in professing loyalty so he first received the rebuke of Jesus for failure to act according to his profession.

title: Matthew 26:44
text: A third time, saying again the same words. A proof of his intense earnestness and anguish.  Contrast this with the 'vain repetitions' of  Matthew 6:7 .

title: Matthew 26:46
text: Let us be going. To meet those who were coming to take him.  It was impossible that the disciples should sleep on.  The sudden appearance of Judas and those with him prevented it.

title: Matthew 26:47
text: A great multitude. It was composed of part of the Jewish Temple guard ( Luke 22:52 ), a detachment of Roman soldiers ( John 18:3 John 18:12 ), servants of the high priest ( Matthew 26:51 ) and probably some of the more bigoted among the elders and chief priests.  The size of the crowd indicated that the power of Jesus was feared.  It was necessary for the Jews to make the Roman governor believe that they were arresting a dangerous political agitator.

title: Matthew 26:48
text: Whomsoever I shall kiss. The kiss, thus debased by Judas to a sign of treachery, was sometimes given by a pupil to a master but more often by a master to a pupil.  In addressing our Lord as Rabbi, or Master, Judas showed that he intended to avail himself of this custom.

title: Matthew 26:50
text: Friend. The Greek word stands for an expression of civility rather than for friendliness.  It was a word often used in reply by a rabbi to a pupil.

title: Matthew 26:51
text:
One of them. Peter.  See  John 18:10 .
 

 
The servant. Malchus ( John 18:10 ).

title: Matthew 26:52
text: All they that take the sword, etc.  In his most perilous hour Jesus fearlessly affirmed in effect that warfare in his behalf must be carried on by the power of the Spirit.

title: Matthew 26:53
text: Twelve legions of angels. Our Lord could have invoked almighty power to save himself, but obediently fulfilled his Father's will as revealed in the Scriptures.

title: Matthew 26:58
text:
Peter followed him afar off. He was evidently the first of the disciples to recover from the terror caused by the arrest of Jesus.
 

 
Unto the court of the high priest. Outside the room into which Jesus was taken for examination.

title: Matthew 26:59
text: Sought false witness against Jesus. It was illegal for judges to seek any witness, but to seek a false witness was infamous.  Both the spirit and the letter of Jewish law were ignored in the proceedings before the Sanhedrin.  Murder was in the hearts of its members.

title: Matthew 26:61
text: I am able to destroy, etc.  These witnesses did not report the words of our Lord correctly.  See  John 2:19-21 .

title: Matthew 26:63
text: Tell us whether thou art the Christ, the Son of God. The attempt to obtain an answer from Jesus having failed through the latter's silence, the high priest asked him the most searching and decisive question that was possible, an affirmative answer to which made any further proof unnecessary.

title: Matthew 26:64
text: Thou hast said. See note on  Matthew 26:25

title: Matthew 26:65
text: Rent his garments. This was according to custom, on proof of a charge of blasphemy.  It would have been contrary to the hostile intention of the high priest or of the Sanhedrin to take any honest step towards investigating the claim of Jesus to be the Christ, the Messiah.

title: Matthew 26:66
text: He is worthy of death. This condemnation was illegal because passed on the same day as the trial.  Jewish law required a delay of one day in such cases.  The trial itself was informal, and it was also illegal because held at night on the eve of the Passover feast.

title: Matthew 26:68
text: Prophesy. At this moment Jesus was blindfolded ( Luke 22:64 ).

title: Matthew 26:70
text: He denied before them all. See  Mark 14:66-72 Luke 22:55-62 John 18:15-18 John 18:25-27 .  The denials of Peter that are recorded by the other three evangelists do not differ from these in essential points.  There are only variations of minor detail, such as would appear in the accounts of witnesses who were intent upon the main issue and the most striking scenes, and therefore not careful about those of less importance.

title: Matthew 26:71
text: Into the porch. The entrance hall from the street.  Beyond this was the court or quadrangle, open to the sky, and around which were built the different rooms of the house of the high priest.

title: Matthew 26:73
text: Thy speech maketh thee known. Peter's Galilean dialect.

title: Matthew 26:75
text:
Peter remembered. See  Mark 14:72 Luke 22:61 .
 

 
He went out, and wept bitterly. Out from the porch or entrance passage into the street.  Repentance and remorse drove him away from the throng.

title: Matthew 27:1
text: When morning was come. This was a formal meeting of the Sanhedrin, held to ratify what had been done at the earlier one and also to consider the execution of the sentence.  The power of life and death was in the Roman authorities.

title: Matthew 27:3
text: Repented himself. Judas repented, but not so as to change his character.  The word used here signifies remorse, not the acceptance of new motives of action.

title: Matthew 27:4
text: What is that to us? The question indicates an abrupt, dismissal of Judas as of one who had been hired and paid for his crime, and therefore had no right to reproach his fellow criminals.  The chief priests and elders had done with Judas.  His remorse was his own affair, not theirs.  But his appearance must have made them extremely uncomfortable.  It was like a threat to reveal their complicity in a disgraceful plot.  They wanted Jesus to be condemned by Pilate without inquiry.  Had Judas been so minded, he might have made serious trouble for them with the Roman governor.

title: Matthew 27:5
text:
Into the sanctuary. The holy place where none but priests had a right to enter.
 

 
Went away and hanged himself. This account of the end of Judas apparently differs in some respects from that given in  Acts 1:18 ; but the two accounts are not necessarily inconsistent, although the materials for reconciling them are lacking.

title: Matthew 27:7
text: The potter's field. According to tradition it was in the valley of Hinnom, south of Jerusalem.

title: Matthew 27:9
text: Through Jeremiah the prophet. The quotation is from  Zechariah 11:12 Zechariah 11:13 ; but it is said to be from Jeremiah because that prophet's name heads the list of prophetical books from which it was taken.

title: Matthew 27:11
text:
Jesus stood before the governor. The narrative of the trial before Pilate given by Matthew is practically the same as that by Mark, Luke and John, though substantially agreeing with the first two evangelists, add several features.  Luke emphasizes the political charges, John the conversations between Jesus and Pilate.
 

 
Art thou the King of the Jews? See  John 18:33-37 .

title: Matthew 27:15
text: Was wont to release. A custom of the Feast of the Passover which recalled the deliverance of the Jews from bondage.  See  John 18:39 .  There is no known Jewish authority for the custom, even although it was in connection with the Passover; but it was probably established by Herod the Great in imitation of the Roman practice of liberating prisoners at certain festivals.

title: Matthew 27:16
text: Barabbas. He had committed a murder during a political insurrection of which he was leader ( Mark 15:7 Luke 23:19 ).

title: Matthew 27:19
text: His wife. Claudia Procula or Procla was her name according to tradition.

title: Matthew 27:20
text: Persuaded the multitudes. The chief priests and elders feared the popularity of Jesus, especially with the Galileans.  Hence they sought to discredit him with the people.

title: Matthew 27:22
text: Let him be crucified. A brutal cry for vengeance.  The Jewish leaders had been first in their desire to kill our Lord and now they had induced the mob, or the majority of the mob, to join them.

title: Matthew 27:24
text: Washed his hands. This is only in Matthew.  It was a Jewish custom, which Pilate knew that all would understand.

title: Matthew 27:25
text: His blood be on us, and on our children. They knew not what they said in uttering these words.  In one sense the sufferings of the Jews ever since bear witness that the prophecy has been terribly fulfilled.

title: Matthew 27:26
text: Jesus he scourged. That is, caused to be scourged.  According to a Roman custom, scourging preceded crucifixion.  The scourge was made of leather thongs, to which were attached sharp pieces of metal or other hard substance.

title: Matthew 27:28
text: A scarlet robe. a sign of royalty.  Mark and John call it purple.

title: Matthew 27:29
text: A reed. A symbol of the kingly sceptre.

title: Matthew 27:31
text: To crucify him. Crucifixion was the most painful and degrading form of punishment known.  It was a custom of the Romans and was introduced by them among the Jews.  The cross was commonly formed of two pieces of wood, one a pole or stake from nine to twelve feet long and fixed in the ground, the other shorter.  The victim's hands were usually nailed to the shorter piece and then he was raised and fastened to the upright stake.  The suffering often lasted for days, death resulting from exhaustion.  See  Mark 15:20 Mark 15:21 Luke 23:26-32 John 19:16 John 19:17 .

title: Matthew 27:32
text:
A man of Cyrene, Simon by name. He was a Jew and the city from which he came was in North Africa.  It contained a large colony of Jews.  Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus, afterwards known in the early church.
 

 
That he might bear his cross. There is a tradition that our Lord fainted under his burden.  Such may have been partly the effect of the scourging, when Simon was compelled to take up the cross.  Mark would seem to indicate that Jesus was exhausted when brought to the place of crucifixion ( Mark 15:21-23 ).

title: Matthew 27:33
text: Golgotha. Aramaic for skull.  This name was given to it either because of the skulls found there, or because the shape of the hill was like that of a skull.

title: Matthew 27:35
text:
When they had crucified him. The cross on which our Lord suffered was of the kind usually shown in illustrations, namely, that in which the shorter beam or stake crosses the longer at right angles and about half way between the top and the center.  This is indicated by the fact that the inscription was put above his head.  Christ was placed upon the cross at the third hour ( Mark 15:25 ), or nine o'clock in the morning.
 

 
They parted his garments, etc.  The garments of a victim of the death sentence were given to his executioners.  Lots were cast because of the seamless coat which the Roman soldiers did not wish to rend ( John 19:24 ).

title: Matthew 27:37
text: His accusation written. The name and crime of an accused person were written on a placard above his head.  In the case of our Lord it was in Hebrew, Greek and Latin ( John 19:20 ).

title: Matthew 27:40
text: Thou that destroyest the temple. See  John 2:21 .

title: Matthew 27:42
text: King of Israel. A title given to Jesus only here and in  Mark 15:32 .

title: Matthew 27:43
text: He trusteth on God. This is nearly identical with the language of  Psalms 22:8 .

title: Matthew 27:45
text: Now from the sixth hour. From twelve or noon until three in the afternoon.

title: Matthew 27:46
text: Eli. This is the Hebrew form; the Aramaic is given in  Mark 15:34 .  This is the fourth of the Seven Words from the cross.  The first is from  Luke 23:34 the second,  Luke 23:43 ; the third,  John 19:26 John 19:27 ; the fifth,  John 19:28 ; the sixth,  John 19:30 ; the seventh,  Luke 23:46 Psalms 31:5 .

title: Matthew 27:47
text: Calleth Elijah. This was probably spoken in derision.

title: Matthew 27:51
text: Rent in two. The veil between the holy place and the holy of holies.  See  Hebrews 10:19 Hebrews 10:20 .

title: Matthew 27:53
text: After his resurrection. Though the tombs had been opened by the earthquake, the dead did not rise from them until after the resurrection of Jesus.

title: Matthew 27:54
text:
The centurion. He commanded the four Roman soldiers who were the guard at the crucifixion.  See  Luke 23:47 .
 

 
Mary Magdalene. The same who had been cured of demoniacal possession ( Luke 8:2 ).  See  Mark 15:40 Mark 15:41 John 19:25 .

title: Matthew 27:57
text: A rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph. A secret follower of Jesus who was a member of the Sanhedrin, but had not taken any part in condemning his Master ( Luke 23:50 Luke 23:51 ).

title: Matthew 27:60
text: Rolled a great stone. Nicodemus helped Joseph in this ( John 19:39-42 ).

title: Matthew 27:61
text: The other Mary. The mother of Joses and James the Less ( Mark 15:47 ).

title: Matthew 27:62
text: The Preparation. Friday, the day before the Sabbath.

title: Matthew 27:64
text: Error. Deceit.

title: Matthew 28:1
text: As it began to dawn. At sunrise ( Mark 16:2 ).

title: Matthew 28:2
text:
A great earthquake. Mentioned only by Matthew.
 

 
An angel of the Lord. See  Luke 24:4 John 20:12 .

title: Matthew 28:4
text: The watchers. The guard of soldiers.

title: Matthew 28:6
text: He is not here, for he is risen. This was clear and decisive as well as joyful news to the wondering women.  The accounts of the other evangelists show that it was hard to convince some of the saddened followers of the Lord that he was indeed risen.  See  John 20:2 John 20:15 John 20:25-29 Luke 24:34-43 .

title: Matthew 28:7
text: He goeth before you into Galilee. Jesus had promised this to his disciples ( Mark 14:28 ).

title: Matthew 28:8
text: Ran to bring his disciples word. The sequence of events concerning the appearance of Jesus to the women was probably as follows: After Mary Magdalene and the other Mary had been spoken to by the angel they ran to tell the disciples.  Peter and John hurried to the tomb and returned.  Then Mary Magdalene, who had also returned to the tomb, lingered after they departed and did not know Jesus when she saw him, mistaking him for the gardener; then Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene a second time, when she was with other women.

title: Matthew 28:10
text: Go tell my brethren that they depart into Galilee. Tell them of my resurrection in order that they may prepare to meet mine Galilee according to my words.

title: Matthew 28:12
text: They gave much money unto the soldiers. The bribery of the guard by the chief priests and elders is told only by Matthew.

title: Matthew 28:14
text: We will persuade him. In the same way as they had persuaded the soldiers-by bribes.

title: Matthew 28:16
text: Unto the mountain. It was probably near Capernaum.  Not only the eleven, but all the disciples of Jesus who were told of his resurrection were most likely gathered there.  It has been held that the words 'my brethren' in  Matthew 28:10  apply generally to all the disciples who could be assembled to meet the Lord.  This appearance of Jesus is therefore that mentioned in  I Corinthians 15:6 .

title: Matthew 28:18
text: All authority hath been given unto me. A sublime affirmation of the victory won through his resurrection.

title: Matthew 28:20
text: Lo, I am with you always. Jesus after his resurrection had proved by his different appearances how he could be with his disciples and yet unseen by them.  After he had triumphed over death they could not doubt his promise to be with them at all times, even unto the end of their lives and of the world.

title: Mark 1:1
text:
The beginning. The opening of Mark's narrative is not concerned with the birth and genealogy of Jesus but with his public ministry.
 

 
Son of God. Mark wrote for the Gentiles; Matthew for the Jews.  Hence the latter sought to prove the Davidic descent of our Lord.  Mark in describing Jesus as the Son of God has the point of view of directly presenting him as the Savior of the world.

title: Mark 1:4
text: In the wilderness. Between Hebron and the Dead Sea.

title: Mark 1:5
text: All the country. All classes of the people: Pharisees and Sadducees ( Matthew 3:7 ), publicans or tax collectors ( Luke 3:12 ), rich and poor ( Luke 3:10 ), and soldiers ( Luke 3:14 ).

title: Mark 1:10
text: He saw. While praying ( Luke 3:21 ).

title: Mark 1:13
text:
Tempted of Satan. 'Satan' means enemy.  In Matthew and Luke he was tempted of the 'devil,' which word means slanderer or false accuser.
 

 
With the wild beasts. This feature of the temptation is mentioned by Mark only.

title: Mark 1:14
text:
Was delivered up. Imprisoned by Herod.  See  Mark 6:17 .
 

 
Came into Galilee. The opening of the Galilean ministry.

title: Mark 1:16
text:
The sea of Galilee. Its other names are the Sea of Tiberias and the Lake of Gennesaret.  In the Old Testament it is called the Sea of Chinnereth or Cinneroth.  It is twelve and three-fourths miles long by seven and a half miles wide.  The water is fresh and clear and fish abound.  The sea is notable for its low level, being 682.5 feet beneath that of the Mediterranean.  It is liable to sudden and violent storms.
 

 
Simon. Afterwards called Peter.  It is significant that Peter's call to be a disciple of Jesus is recorded thus early by Mark.  This gospel was founded mainly on Peter's reminiscences.  Peter and his brother Andrew lived at Bethsaida on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee.  See  Matthew 4:18-22 .

title: Mark 1:19
text: With the hired servants. Zebedee was not a poor man.  It is a mistake to suppose that the occupation of a fisherman in Galilee in the time of Christ indicated any unusual poverty or ignorance.

title: Mark 1:21
text: Capernaum. See note on  Matthew 4:13 .

title: Mark 1:22
text: As having authority. The teaching of Jesus completely reversed the method of the scribes.  The latter narrowly interpreted the letter of the law; Jesus affirmed principles by which even the law itself was to be judged.  See note on  Matthew 7:29 .

title: Mark 1:23
text:
Their synagogue. See note on  Matthew 4:23 .
 

 
A man with an unclean spirit. Literally, in an unclean spirit.  In Luke he is spoken of as having the spirit of an unclean demon ( Mark 4:33 ).

title: Mark 1:24
text: I know thee. A clear recognition of Jesus as the Messiah.

title: Mark 1:29
text: They. The four who had been called ( Mark 1:16-20 ).

title: Mark 1:30
text: Sick of a fever. A dangerous and violent malady, as seems to be indicated by  Luke 4:38 .

title: Mark 1:32
text: When the sun did set. After the heat of the day when the sick could be brought more comfortably to Jesus.

title: Mark 1:33
text: At the door. Of Peter's house.  Peter and his brother Andrew, whose permanent home was Bethsaida, were at that time living in Capernaum.

title: Mark 1:35
text:
A great while before day. At the earliest dawn.
 

 
Into a desert place, and there prayed. A season of solitary communion with God naturally following a day of self-denying labor.  It was our Lord's habit to prepare by prayer for the work that lay before him.  Many of these holy seasons of quiet were spent by him around the shores of the Sea of Galilee, where desert places were near.

title: Mark 1:38
text:
Into the next towns. At this time there was a crowded population in Galilee.  The towns and cities were numerous.  Chorazin, Bethsaida, Magdala and many other populous places were not far from Capernaum.  Jesus could not submit to excessive calls upon his miraculous powers at any one place when multitudes elsewhere needed his preaching.
 

 
For to this end came I forth. Note the emphasis of his preaching, a greater work than performing miracles.

title: Mark 1:40
text: There cometh to him a leper. In the East leprosy was the most terrible of diseases, incurable then as now.  The nature of his affliction compelled him to wander about alone, shunned like a wild beast.  See note on  Matthew 8:2-4 .

title: Mark 1:45
text: Began to publish it much. The astounding cure of the leper could not be kept secret, and the news spread so rapidly that the eager crowds made it appear as if some political agitator required the notice of the authorities.  Jesus wished to avoid this, as at that time Galilee was in a turbulent and rebellious condition.

title: Mark 2:2
text: Spake the word. Was teaching.

title: Mark 2:4
text: Uncovered the roof. The dwelling houses of Palestine usually had a flight of stone steps built on the outside and leading to the roof.  In this case the four who carried the paralytic in his bed up to the roof lifted enough of the thin stone tiling to lower the bed through the opening.

title: Mark 2:5
text: Thy sins are forgiven. See note on  Matthew 9:2-5 .

title: Mark 2:12
text:
Before them all. As if the crowd had been awed by the miracle that had been performed and instinctively made way for the healed man.
 

 
On this fashion. Jesus had astonished the crowd by healing the paralytic; but more especially were the scribes confounded by his assumption of the power to forgive sins.  He challenged them to deny this, in effect declaring that it was as easy for him to forgive sins as it was to cure disease.

title: Mark 2:14
text: Levi. See note on  Matthew 9:9 .  'Matthew', or 'Mattathias', means the gift of God.

title: Mark 2:15
text: Many publicans and sinners. Matthew himself having been a publican, it was natural that publicans should be among his guests.  Their reputation may be guessed from the fact that they and sinners are mentioned in the same breath.  The publicans here spoken of were the lesser native collectors of taxes, subject to Roman officials.  They were notorious for merciless greed.

title: Mark 2:16
text: Said unto his disciples, etc.  It was significant that this objection by the scribes was made to the disciples and not to their Master.  Jesus had just vindicated his claims in a manner that discouraged interference.  It was easier to annoy his disciples.

title: Mark 2:18
text: John's disciples and the Pharisees. See note on  Matthew 9:14 .

title: Mark 2:19
text: While the bridegroom is with them. See note on  Matthew 9:15 .

title: Mark 2:20
text: Then will they fast. See note on  Matthew 9:15 .

title: Mark 2:21
text: Undressed cloth. See note on  Matthew 9:16 .

title: Mark 2:25
text: What David did. See note on  Matthew 12:3 .

title: Mark 3:2
text: They watched him. They had followed and closely observed him for some time with the design of securing grounds of legal accusation against him.

title: Mark 3:5
text:
Looked round about on them with anger. Implying a deliberate and penetrating gaze that was intended for each and all.  The anger was that of holy indignation deeply touched with grief.
 

 
Being grieved. Though righteously angry, our Lord yet had the deepest compassion for their hardness of heart, a condition more hopeless than they realized.

title: Mark 3:6
text: With the Herodians took counsel. The Herodians were political adherents of Herod the Great and his successors.  The Pharisees were bitterly hostile to them, and the willingness of the former to join thus with their enemies shows how deep was their hatred of Jesus.

title: Mark 3:7
text: Withdrew See note on  Matthew 12:15 .

title: Mark 3:8
text:
Idumea. The district south of Judea and the Dead Sea.
 

 
Beyond Jordan. This district was Gentile with a mixed population.

title: Mark 3:11
text:
Thou art the Son of God. The Messiah.
 

 
That they should not make him known. The fame of his teaching and miracles had so spread that the people were likely to be attracted to him as a political deliverer.  The thought of Jesus was far from this.  Besides, he was about to appoint the twelve disciples.

title: Mark 3:17
text: Boanerges. James and John were men of exceptional force of character and eloquence.  The former was sometimes called James the Great.

title: Mark 3:18
text:
Bartholomew. Nathanael of Cana of Galilee ( John 1:45 John 21:2 ).
 

 
The son of Alphaeus. James the son of Alphaeus was called James the Less or the Little.
 

 
Thaddeus. This was his surname.  In Luke he is mentioned as Judas the son of James ( Mark 6:16 ).

title: Mark 3:20
text: So much as eat bread. This is a graphic detail that was most probably taken by Mark from Peter's reminiscences.

title: Mark 3:21
text: He is beside himself. His friends thought that his excessive zeal in his work was likely to deprive him of self-control.

title: Mark 3:22
text:
The scribes. The same enemies who had been watching him for days.
 

 
The prince of the demons. See note on  Matthew 12:24 .

title: Mark 3:24
text: If a kingdom be divided against itself. See note on  Matthew 12:25 .

title: Mark 3:27
text: Except he first bind the strong man. See note on  Matthew 12:29 .

title: Mark 3:29
text: Shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit. See note on  Matthew 12:31 .

title: Mark 3:31
text: His brethren. See  Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 .

title: Mark 3:35
text: For whosoever shall do the will of God. See note on  Matthew 12:50 .

title: Mark 4:2
text: Many things in parables. See notes on  Matthew 13:3 .

title: Mark 4:3
text: The sower. See notes on  Matthew 13:3 .

title: Mark 4:11
text: The mystery of the kingdom of God. See note on  Matthew 13:11 .

title: Mark 4:12
text: That seeing they may see. 'Seeing they see not.'  See note on  Matthew 13:13 .

title: Mark 4:13
text: Know ye not this parable? As if it were not easily understood without on interpretation.

title: Mark 4:14
text: The sower soweth the word. Christ, the sower of the seed of divine truth.

title: Mark 4:15
text: The way side. The hard, trodden road.

title: Mark 4:21
text:
The lamp. See note on  Matthew 5:15 .
 

 
The bushel. See note on  Matthew 5:15 .

title: Mark 4:24
text: With what measure ye mete. Ye shall increase in spiritual knowledge according to your attentiveness and diligence.

title: Mark 4:25
text: He that hath not. See note on  Matthew 25:28 .

title: Mark 4:26
text: As if a man should cast seed upon the earth. Mark is the only one of the evangelists who records this parable.  'A man' here means Christ, and 'the earth' is the spiritual nature and needs of man.

title: Mark 4:27
text: He knoweth not how. He does not understand the unseen power by which the seed grows, and which is constantly taking effect.

title: Mark 4:28
text: First the blade. The gradual unfolding of the plant counsels patience in the development of character.

title: Mark 4:31
text: Like a grain of mustard seed. See note on  Matthew 13:31 .

title: Mark 4:35
text: The other side. The east side of the Sea of Galilee.

title: Mark 4:38
text: Carest thou not that we perish? See note on  Matthew 8:25 .

title: Mark 5:1
text: The Gerasenes. Or Gadarenes.  See notes on Mt 8.28.

title: Mark 5:2
text: Out of the tombs. See notes on  Matthew 8:28 .

title: Mark 5:7
text:
Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God. See notes on  Matthew 8:29 .
 

 
Torment me not. See notes on  Matthew 8:29 .

title: Mark 5:9
text: My name is Legion. The word 'Legion' is used because it expressed the popular idea of great numbers.  In the New Testament period a Roman legion included ten cohorts of six centuries each.  A cohort contained six hundred men; a century, one hundred men.

title: Mark 5:11
text: A great herd of swine feeding. As swine were an abomination to the Jews, the fact that there was such a herd at large suggests the wild and uncivilized nature of the district.

title: Mark 5:15
text: Clothed in his right mind. The man was naked when Jesus commanded the unclean spirit to leave him ( Luke 8:27 ).

title: Mark 5:17
text: To depart from their borders. Probably among those who besought him to depart were the owners of the swine, who were troubled over their loss.

title: Mark 5:18
text: Besought him that he might be with him. This appeal of the man who was now restored to reason was unspeakably pathetic.  No wonder that he wished to be with his divine Deliverer.

title: Mark 5:20
text: Decapolis. See note on  Matthew 4:25 .  Decapolis was a district containing the following ten cities: Damascus, Philadelphia, Raphana, Scythopolis, Gadara, Hippus, Dium, Pella, Gerasa, Canatha.

title: Mark 5:22
text: One of the rulers of the synagogue. See note on  Matthew 9:18 .

title: Mark 5:25
text: A woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years. While Jesus was on his way to the bedside of the daughter of Jairus, he was timidly approached by this woman, whose meekness and modesty would not permit her to press forward boldly toward him.  Her touch of humble, quiet faith contrasts with the crowding of the throng.

title: Mark 5:29
text: And straightway. She was healed even before Jesus spoke to her.  See note on  Matthew 9:20 .

title: Mark 5:32
text: And he looked round about to see. He looked round in expectant love to see her who so humbly trusted in him.  Not long before he had looked round in holy indignation, yet in compassionate grief, upon the hard-hearted Pharisees ( Mark 3:5 ).

title: Mark 5:36
text: Fear not, only believe In his miracles our Lord insists with tremendous force upon the necessity of faith for those who would be healed.  So here he ignores the report of the death of the ruler's little daughter and turns to the ruler himself, concerned only about the latter's faith.

title: Mark 5:39
text: Why make ye a tumult, and weep? Part of the tumult and weeping did not signify real grief.  See note on  Matthew 9:23 .

title: Mark 5:40
text: They laughed him to scorn. See note on  Matthew 9:24 .

title: Mark 5:41
text: Talitha cumi. This and other expressions in Aramaic, a Hebrew dialect, go to show that it was the language commonly spoken by our Lord.  See  Mark 7:34 Matthew 27:46 .

title: Mark 5:42
text: They were amazed straightway. The word 'amazed' here expresses an almost helpless wonder.  It was a wholesome reaction from the jeering scorn and doubt with which they had at first greeted our Lord.

title: Mark 6:1
text: His own country. His second visit to Nazareth.  He was treated in the same manner on his first visit ( Luke 4:16-30 ).  There is no record of his ever having been in Nazareth again.

title: Mark 6:3
text: Is not this the carpenter, etc.  The description of our Lord as 'the carpenter' is peculiar to Mark.  In Matthew he is spoken of as 'the carpenter's son' ( Matthew 13:55 ).  There is an old tradition that Jesus made yokes and ploughs.

title: Mark 6:7
text: Authority over the unclean spirits. To that extent he imparted to his disciples his power of working miracles.

title: Mark 6:8
text: Wallet. Made of leather to contain food, and carried over the shoulder.

title: Mark 6:9
text: Sandals. Made of bark, usually of the palm tree.

title: Mark 6:10
text: Wheresoever ye enter. They were to abide in the house which received them.  Matthew adds that they were to salute it ( Mark 10:12 ).

title: Mark 6:11
text: Shake off the dust that is under your feet. This was to be a witness against those who rejected Christ.  See note on  Matthew 10:14 .  Paul did this on two notable occasions.  See  Acts 13:51 Acts 18:6 .

title: Mark 6:14
text: King Herod. Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Iturea and Perea.  He was the son of Herod the Great.

title: Mark 6:16
text: John, whom I beheaded, he is risen. Superstition and remorse led Herod to believe that the man whom he had murdered had risen from the dead.  As a thoroughgoing Sadducee in his sympathy Herod did not believe in the resurrection, but his troubled conscience overcame his disbelief.

title: Mark 6:17
text: For the sake of Herodias. See note on  Matthew 14:3 .

title: Mark 6:22
text: Daughter of Herodias. Salome.  See note on  Matthew 14:6 .

title: Mark 6:24
text: What shall I ask? This was the opportunity for revenge that Herodias longed for.  See notes on  Matthew 14:3 Matthew 14:6 Matthew 14:8 .

title: Mark 6:26
text: The king was exceeding sorry. A proof of his high regard for John.  Though depraved himself, he recognized the strength and loftiness of the prophet's character.  See note on  Matthew 14:9 .

title: Mark 6:27
text: In the prison. At Machaerus, where a fort and prison had been built.  It was about five miles east of the Dead Sea.

title: Mark 6:30
text: And the apostles gather themselves together. This was their return to Capernaum to tell the Master about the results of their first mission.

title: Mark 6:31
text: No leisure so much as to eat. Besides those assembled to hear our Lord and to be healed, Capernaum was now crowded with pilgrims on their way to the Passover feast at Jerusalem ( John 6:4 ).  From the excessive toil thus caused Jesus called the apostles to rest themselves.

title: Mark 6:32
text: To a desert place apart. Near Bethsaida Julias, a few miles northeast of the Sea of Galilee.  This town was originally called Bethsaida.  It had been greatly improved and enlarged by the tetrarch Herod Philip, who gave it the additional name of Julias in honor of the daughter of the Roman emperor.

title: Mark 6:35
text: The place is desert. It was probably uninhabited, but not all sandy waste.  See  Mark 6:39 .

title: Mark 6:38
text: Five, and two fishes. They found that a lad had five barley loaves and two small fishes ( John 6:9 ).

title: Mark 6:40
text: In ranks. In groups.

title: Mark 6:44
text: Were five thousand men. Matthew says, 'about five thousand men, besides women and children.'  See note on  Matthew 14:21 .  According to custom the women and children would stand or sit separate from the men.

title: Mark 6:45
text:
And straightway he constrained his disciples. No time was to be lost in preventing the multitude, who were astounded by this miracle, from forcibly attempting to make him king.  See  John 6:14 John 6:15 .  Therefore he sent the disciples by boat across the lake while he dispersed the people.
 

 
Bethsaida. Not Bethsaida Julias, but a place west of Capernaum ( John 6:17 ).

title: Mark 6:46
text: Into the mountain to pray. See note on  Matthew 14:23 .

title: Mark 6:47
text: In the midst of the sea. The contrary winds prevented them from sailing more than half way across ( John 6:19 ).

title: Mark 6:48
text:
The fourth watch. Three o'clock in the morning.
 

 
Walking on the sea. Like the feeding of the five thousand, this miracle was a direct mastery of the powers of nature.

title: Mark 6:51
text: And the wind ceased. Matthew's account of this miracle includes Peter's attempt to walk upon the sea ( Mark 14:28-30 ).

title: Mark 6:53
text: The land unto Gennesaret. On the northwestern shore of the Sea of Galilee.  It is a plain, three miles long by one wide and remarkable fertile.

title: Mark 7:1
text: Who had come from Jerusalem. The Pharisees and scribes had been keeping the Passover feast and now returned to watch Jesus.

title: Mark 7:2
text: Unwashen hands. That is, not washed according to the ceremonial manner practiced by the Pharisees.  It does mean that the disciples failed in the cleanliness resulting from the ordinary Jewish custom of washing by pouring water upon the hands.

title: Mark 7:3
text: The tradition of the elders. The Pharisees sometimes set the tradition of the elders above the law itself.  See note on  Matthew 15:2 .

title: Mark 7:8
text: The commandment of God. Jesus answered their accusation of violating the tradition of the elders by charging them with rejecting the commandment of God.  See note on  Matthew 15:3 .

title: Mark 7:13
text: By your tradition. The unwritten law, or tradition, was derived from the elders, to whom it was said to have been given in charge by Moses.  Moses was said to have received it orally from God.  The Pharisees had in this case ( Mark 7:11 Mark 7:12 ) so exalted tradition that the word of God had been made void.

title: Mark 7:15
text: There is nothing from without, etc.  Our Lord here contrasts external form and ceremony with the secret thoughts of the heart.  See note on  Matthew 15:11 .

title: Mark 7:22
text: An evil eye. The disposition that is revealed in the look of jealous hatred.

title: Mark 7:24
text: He arose, and went away. The bitter opposition of the Pharisees and scribes caused him to do so.  He had to seek a more fruitful field of labor.  Accordingly he left the district around Capernaum and went northwesterly into the borders of Phoenicia.

title: Mark 7:25
text: Having heard of him. There was hardly any inhabited district of Palestine, and but few on its borders, into which the fame of Jesus had not gone.  See  Mark 3:7 Mark 3:8 .

title: Mark 7:26
text: A Syrophoenician by race. That is, a Phoenician belonging to the Roman province of Syria.  See note on  Matthew 15:22 .

title: Mark 7:27
text:
The children. The Jews
 

 
The dogs. Or little dogs.  The term applied by the Jews to the heathen.  An epithet commonly used by Mohammedans today against Christians is, 'dog of an infidel.'

title: Mark 7:28
text: Even the dogs. The woman, believing in Jesus and thinking only of her daughter's affliction, willingly accepts this description of her race, not knowing that her faith was being tested.

title: Mark 7:30
text: And the demon gone out. This miracle was one of those in which the person cured was distant.  See  Luke 7:6 John 4:46-54 .

title: Mark 7:32
text:
Deaf, and had an impediment in his speech. Though deaf, the man was not entirely dumb.
 

 
They beseech. The afflicted man was brought to Jesus by his friends, who had to make a way for him through the crowd and speak for him.  See  Mark 2:3-5 .

title: Mark 7:33
text: Put his fingers into his ears, and he spat. This was evidently done to help the man understand that his cure was being effected.  He could only be made to comprehend by signs.  It was only after this that Jesus cured him.

title: Mark 7:34
text: Ephphatha. See note on  Mark 5:41 .

title: Mark 8:1
text: Again a great multitude, etc.  Brought together by the fame of the miracles.  That the multitude was mainly heathen is evident from the known race and religion of the Decapolis district, and also from the expression 'they glorified the God of Israel' in  Matthew 15:31 .

title: Mark 8:4
text: Whence shall one be able. A strange and careless question for the disciples to ask, especially after the feeding of the five thousand.

title: Mark 8:6
text: He commandeth the multitude to sit down. In a desert place on the east side of the Sea of Galilee.  See  Matthew 15:33 .

title: Mark 8:8
text: They ate and were filled. For comparison with the miracle of feeding the five thousand see note on  Matthew 15:37 .

title: Mark 8:10
text: Into the parts of Dalmanutha. The region about Magdala on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

title: Mark 8:11
text:
And the Pharisees came forth. They had evidently been waiting for his return.  They wished to resume their malicious questioning with a view to silencing him.  This time some Sadducees joined them ( Matthew 16:1 ).
 

 
A sign from heaven. Jesus had confounded them by his miracles of healing; now they wanted to test him in a different way.  They asked for some appearance in the sky, some portentous and dazzling wonder such as Elijah and Samuel had wrought by God's power.

title: Mark 8:12
text:
He sighed deeply. In mingled grief and compassion over their willful blindness and hardness of heart.
 

 
There shall no sign be given. He looked upon their question as a temptation and refused to consider it.  See  Matthew 12:39-41 .

title: Mark 8:13
text: The other side. The eastern side of the Sea of Galilee.

title: Mark 8:15
text:
The leaven of the Pharisees. Hypocrisy and deceit.
 

 
The leaven of Herod. Worldliness.  See note on  Matthew 16:6-12 .

title: Mark 8:21
text: Do ye not yet understand? Can ye not interpret my words spiritually?

title: Mark 8:22
text: Bethsaida. Bethsaida Julias.

title: Mark 8:23
text: He took hold of the blind man. Jesus led him apart from the crowd and wrought the cure gradually, and he did in the case of the deaf man with the impediment in his speech.  The man's friends had besought Jesus to heal him by a touch, but this was denied.

title: Mark 8:27
text: The villages of Caesarea Philippi. The parts or regions.  See note on  Matthew 16:13 .

title: Mark 8:28
text: Elijah. See note on  Matthew 16:14 .

title: Mark 8:29
text:
But who say ye that I am? A test of the spiritual insight of his disciples.  See note on  Matthew 16:15 .
 

 
Thou art the Christ. The great fact of Peter's confession is here given more briefly than in  Matthew 16:16 Luke 9:20 .  It is noteworthy that Mark, who wrote under the guidance of Peter, omits any reference to the latter's being the rock on which Christ's church was to be built.  See note on  Matthew 16:16 .

title: Mark 8:31
text: That the Son of man must suffer many things. It was new and strange teaching for the disciples.  Thus far, although there had been toil, privation and persecution, victory had always been on the side of the Master.  Now he began to talk to them in a way that, to their inadequate foresight, suggested defeat.  They could not understand him and were troubled.

title: Mark 8:33
text: Get thee behind me, Satan. Our Lord looked upon Peter's well meant but presumptuous words as a temptation.  The words 'turning about, and seeing his disciples' indicate that the manner of the rebuke was open and deliberate, as its language was severe.

title: Mark 8:34
text: And take up his cross. See note on  Matthew 10:38 .

title: Mark 8:35
text:
Shall lose it. See note on  Matthew 10:39 .
 

 
Shall save it. See note on  Matthew 10:39 .

title: Mark 9:2
text:
After six days. After Peter's confession; but see  Luke 9:28 .
 

 
A high mountain apart. See notes on  Matthew 17:1 .
 

 
He was transfigured before them. That they might see him in his majesty and glory and be thereby comforted at the time of his humiliation and death.

title: Mark 9:4
text:
,5
 
Elijah with Moses. Representing the law and the prophets.
 

 
Were talking with Jesus. The facts that he was seen by the three apostles at once, and that he was also heard talking with them, prove the reality of the event.
 

 
Let us make three tabernacles. Peter said this in his usual impulsive way.  He was awed by the vision, and wished to take some action in order that its beauty and glory might remain.

title: Mark 9:7
text: Hear ye him. To him is committed all authority.  See note on  Matthew 17:5 .

title: Mark 9:10
text: Questioning among themselves. Mark alone of the evangelists mentions this debate among the three.  They were troubled only about the death and resurrection of their Master.  Jesus had already told them of his approaching sufferings.  Immediately after this vision of surpassing glory he had spoken of his rising again from the dead.  The words added to their perplexity.

title: Mark 9:13
text: Elijah is come. In the person of John the Baptist ( Matthew 17:13 ).

title: Mark 9:15
text: Were greatly amazed. As if the glory of his transfiguration was yet visible in his countenance.

title: Mark 9:17
text: My son, who hath a dumb spirit. He was an only son ( Luke 9:38 ).  His affliction was epilepsy, a disease of the brain, which causes person affected with it to fall down suddenly.  See note on  Matthew 17:15 .

title: Mark 9:18
text: They were not able. The humiliation of their failure must have been deepened by the fact that the scribes were present.

title: Mark 9:19
text: O faithless generation. Our Lord meant not only those before him, but the Jews of his time.

title: Mark 9:23
text:
If thou canst! Not an expression of anger, but spoken to remind the father of the epileptic that doubt was not permissible if a cure was looked for.
 

 
All things, etc.  Another of the many solemn affirmations of Jesus as to the necessity of faith.

title: Mark 9:28
text: Asked him privately. They were sorely perplexed, for Jesus had given them power to do that which in this case they had failed to do.  See  Matthew 10:1 Luke 9:1 .

title: Mark 9:29
text: This kind. Our Lord replied in effect that some forms of demoniac possession were more malignant and difficult than others.  The disciples had not sufficiently considered this.

title: Mark 9:30
text: They went forth from thence. From the region of Mount Hermon in the north down through upper Galilee on the way to Capernaum.  They went as privately as possible on account of the watchfulness of the scribes and Pharisees.

title: Mark 9:31
text: The Son of man is delivered up. The prediction of his suffering, death and resurrection.

title: Mark 9:32
text: Were afraid to ask him. Through grief and dismay at the disappointment of all their hopes.  They did not expect that his Messiahship would lead to his death.

title: Mark 9:35
text: If any man would be first. The fact that Peter, James and John had been selected to witness the transfiguration was not without its natural effect upon them.  They disputed as to whom was the greatest.  Jesus decided by reproving them because of the wrong principle of ambition, which actuated them.  He taught them to measure greatness by the test of devoted, humble service.  See note on  Matthew 18:1 .

title: Mark 9:38
text: We saw one casting out demons. A private and unknown disciple of Jesus, whose faith had been so strengthened by the example of the Master that he was able to perform this miracle in his name.

title: Mark 9:39
text: Forbid him not. Christ's words are a rebuke to the spirit of narrow exclusiveness in the exercise of spiritual gifts.  The disciples should have welcomed the man as a brother worker instead of showing jealousy of his success.

title: Mark 9:42
text: These little ones. See note on  Matthew 18:10 .

title: Mark 9:48
text: Where their worm dieth not. The remorse and torment of the ungodly.

title: Mark 9:49
text: Every one shall be salted with fire. Shall be preserved and purified by a life of spiritual endeavor and achievement, or, on the other hand, shall be compelled to endure the salt of affliction and retribution for persistence in evil ways.

title: Mark 10:1
text: Beyond the Jordan. Perea.  Between the end of chapter 9 and the beginning of chapter 10 Mark omits several events.  See note on  Matthew 19:3 .

title: Mark 10:2
text: Is it lawful, etc.  See note on  Matthew 19:3 .

title: Mark 10:5
text: For your hardness of heart. Christ rebukes their false standard as to the sacredness of the marriage relation.  See note on  Matthew 19:8 .

title: Mark 10:9
text: What therefore God hath joined together. See note on  Matthew 19:6 .

title: Mark 10:10
text: And in the house. Perplexed by the moral rigor and purity of Christ's commands, the disciples sought more light on the question.  They had already done so on more than one occasion ( Mark 9:28 Mark 9:29 Mark 9:33-37 ).  They themselves had been brought up in a more lax view of marriage than that announced authoritatively by our Lord.  See note on  Matthew 19:10 .

title: Mark 10:13
text: Bringing unto him little children. According to custom.  See notes on  Matthew 19:13 Matthew 19:14 .

title: Mark 10:17
text: There ran one to him. The rich young man who had kept the commandments, but lacked the courage to sell all he had and give to the poor.  See notes on  Matthew 19:16 Matthew 19:21 .

title: Mark 10:24
text: How hard is it for them that trust in riches. This utterance of our Lord regarding the destructive power of riches on the spiritual life is even more emphatic than the words in  Matthew 19:23-25 , or in  Luke 18:1-43 Luke 18:24 Luke 18:25 .  It points out the reason why it is so difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God-because his trust is in his riches.  See notes on  Matthew 19:16-24 .

title: Mark 10:26
text: They were astonished exceedingly. The compassion of Jesus for all who suffered, and his tender care of his disciples, often seemed to the latter in sharp contrast to the inflexible severity of his moral principles and commands.  But when they were thus astonished and perplexed, he was always ready to point out the way of escape, as in  Mark 10:27 .  See notes on  Matthew 19:25 .

title: Mark 10:28
text: Peter began to say. Peter's words here seem to indicate that he too was not free from the taint of undue love of riches.  He asked, evidently not with the highest motive, 'what then shall we have?' ( Matthew 19:27 ).  The reply of Jesus affirms all the fullness of earthly as well as heavenly reward for those who are true to him; but he adds, 'with persecutions.'

title: Mark 10:32
text:
On the way. The main road that led to Jerusalem.
 

 
Was going before them. In the position of authority as well as danger--leader, guide, shepherd.  He was proceeding to the scene of his suffering and death.

title: Mark 10:33
text: Shall deliver him unto the Gentiles. It was the Roman power that carried out the sentence of death.  See note on  Matthew 20:18 .

title: Mark 10:37
text: Grant unto us. See notes on  Matthew 20:20 Matthew 20:21 .

title: Mark 10:40
text: For whom it hath been prepared. That is, the question you ask does not now concern your position and your needs and will be finally decided in due time.

title: Mark 10:41
text: Began to be moved with indignation. At the presumption of James and John in trying to secure the highest position for themselves.  Their father Zebedee was wealthier than the parents of the other apostles, and probably they considered that they had stronger claims to advancement.

title: Mark 10:43
text: It is not so among you. You are not to imitate the cruel pride of force and brutal authority which obtains among the Gentiles.  You are under a higher law, the law of unselfish service.

title: Mark 10:45
text: A ransom for many. The supreme proof of his right to be ruler in the kingdom of God.  He gave most for us, therefore most righteously does he rule over us.  See notes on  Matthew 20:28 .

title: Mark 10:46
text: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar Matthew says there were two blind men.  Only one is mentioned here, probably because he was better known.  See notes on  Matthew 20:29 Matthew 20:30 Matthew 20:34 .

title: Mark 11:1
text:
He sendeth two of his disciples. It is not certain who they were; but the details given indicate an attentive eyewitness.  Most probably Peter, on whom Mark depended for his narrative, was one, and the other may have been James or John.   Mark 11:2-9 
 

 
A colt. See notes on  Matthew 21:2 Matthew 21:3 Matthew 21:5 Matthew 21:7-10 .

title: Mark 11:10
text: The kingdom of our father David. A proof that they were entirely ignorant, perhaps with the exception of a few, of the true character of the Messiah.  They still thought that Jesus intended to restore the earthly kingdom of David.

title: Mark 11:11
text:
He entered into Jerusalem. The city was thronged in the streets and on the housetops.  The scribes and Pharisees, and all the friends of the party of Herod and the Sadducees, must have fully realized at last the great power of Jesus over the multitude.  They must have feared deeply for the safety of the beliefs and institutions, which they championed.
 

 
Into the temple. But before this he uttered his lament over the beloved and doomed city ( Luke 19:41-44 ).

title: Mark 11:14
text: No man eat fruit from thee. See  Matthew 21:19  and note thereon.

title: Mark 11:15
text: He entered into the temple. This is to be distinguished from the entry into the Temple recorded in  Mark 11:11 .  See notes on  Matthew 21:12 .

title: Mark 11:18
text: All the multitude was astonished. They were on the verge of making a great public demonstration in his behalf.  This explains the fear of the chief priests and scribes.

title: Mark 11:19
text: Went forth out of the city. Showing his perfect fearlessness in the most imminent danger.

title: Mark 11:20
text: In the morning. On Tuesday, the day following the cleansing of the temple.

title: Mark 11:23
text: And shall not doubt in his heart. Whose faith shall remain steadfast and clear, even in the inmost recesses of the soul.  See  Matthew 17:20 Luke 17:6 .

title: Mark 11:24
text: All things whatsoever ye pray and ask for, etc.  A-never-to-be-surpassed statement of the meaning of faith and prayer.  It is only the union of faith with prayer that produces results.  No petition made in doubt or despair can be answered.  Christ himself declares that in order that we may have or possess the things we ask for, we must first believe that God grants them.

title: Mark 11:28
text: By what authority doest thou these things? There is no record that Jesus was ever ordained as a rabbi.  If not, he had no official authority to teach, according to the requirements of Jewish custom.  It was his authority to call himself the Son of God and to do mighty works about which his enemies questioned him.  See notes on  Matthew 21:23 .

title: Mark 11:33
text: We know not. See note on  Matthew 21:27 .

title: Mark 12:1
text:
24
 
For this cause that ye err. See note on  Matthew 22:29 .

title: Mark 12:12
text: They sought to lay hold on him. See note on  Matthew 21:46 .

title: Mark 12:13
text: Certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians. The Pharisees were probably selected for their ability and willingness to make the attempt to ensnare Jesus by some hoped-for admission on his part.  With regard to the Herodians, see note on  Matthew 22:16 .

title: Mark 12:17
text:
Render unto Caesar, etc.  See note on  Matthew 22:21 .
 

 
And they marveled greatly. See note on  Matthew 22:22 .

title: Mark 12:18
text: There come unto him Sadducees. Hitherto they had not been active in their hostility to Jesus, as the Pharisees had been.  They had the chief places in Jewish society, and were worldly-minded and indifferent to religious agitation.  But now they deemed it prudent to take at least an intellectual, if not a critical, interest in the teaching of our Lord.

title: Mark 12:25
text: As angels in heaven. See note on  Matthew 22:30 .

title: Mark 12:28
text:
One of the scribes. He was a Pharisee and a lawyer ( Matthew 22:34 Matthew 22:35 ).
 

 
What commandment is the first of all. This questioner, who was fair-minded, had been moved to admiration by the replies of Jesus to those who had tried to entangle him in an argument.

title: Mark 12:29
text:
:34
 
The first is, etc.  See notes on  Matthew 22:38 Matthew 22:39 .

title: Mark 12:35
text: How say the scribes that the Christ is the son of David? Jesus here introduced a topic with which every Jew was more or less familiar.  He who claimed to be the Christ, or Messiah, had first of all to prove his Davidic descent.  That the Christ must be the son of David was not only a prevalent religious belief, but it was patriotic politics.

title: Mark 12:36
text:
,37
 
The Lord said, etc.  See notes on  Matthew 22:42-45 .

title: Mark 12:38
text:
:40
 
Beware, etc.  See notes on  Matthew 23:2-5 Matthew 23:7 .  The denunciation of the scribes here is not so severe as in Matthew, but has the same general meaning and object.

title: Mark 12:42
text:
There came a poor widow. Jesus had just spoken ( Mark 12:40 ) about the scribes who devoured widows' houses, that is, abused the confidence of poor widows of whose property they were legal guardians; and now the sight of this widow casting into the treasury all she had moved him to profound sympathy.
 

 
Two mites. About equal to three-tenths of a cent; but this would not be a reliable indication of their purchasing power in our Lord's time.

title: Mark 12:43
text: Cast in more than all, etc.  A righteous and final estimate of her pious act.

title: Mark 13:1
